hens_rule_text: Up to 6 hens at a single-family detached home, guaranteed statewide by Arizona HB 2325 (2024, ARS 9-462.12) for lots of half an acre or less; Peoria's own code (Chapter 16, Animals) defers to this state law for fowl-keeping.
permit_notes: No source found stating a Peoria-specific fowl permit; state law framework focuses on coop/placement standards rather than a permit, but this was not confirmed on an official Peoria page.
setback_notes: Secondary sources describe coop placement at least 20 ft from the property line and 40 ft from a neighboring residence; state law (HB 2325) separately requires at least 20 ft from neighboring dwellings, max 200 sq ft, 8 ft high. Peoria zoning also applies its normal accessory-building setback rules (Secs. 21-410/21-411) to fowl structures.
coop_rules: Enclosed coop, maximum 200 sq ft and 8 ft tall per state law, must be cleaned at least twice a week; accessory buildings for fowl otherwise follow the same setback as the principal building or Secs. 21-410/21-411, whichever is greater.
zoning_notes: Arizona HB 2325 (2024) bars cities and counties from banning up to 6 hens at a detached single-family home on a lot of half an acre or less; Peoria's Chapter 16 (Animals) and its TA24-02 zoning text amendment (backyard fowl + ADUs) were updated to defer to this state floor, referencing ARS 9-462.10/9-462.12. Local rules on roosters, coop placement and cleanliness still apply.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Peoria City Code Ch. 16 (Animals); Zoning Ordinance Secs. 21-410/21-411; state law ARS 9-462.12 (HB 2325)
